_comment: Narration for ielts-068 (P5: IELTS #01, three vocabulary items). Source: js/data/packs/ielts.js, author socrates, topic Health. Teach: 'in deadly earnest' (phrase), 'debatable', 'frivolous'. HANDOFF RULE: the note goes at the nearest punctuation boundary at or after the vocabulary's last word. 'earnest.' and 'debatable.' end their sentence (no comma/colon before the sentence end), so those two are plain segments with the note after the whole sentence (an `after` there would be an error). frivolousSent has the colon right after 'frivolous', so `after: "frivolous"` resolves to 'frivolous:' - frivolousLead + frivolousRest, one TTS take. Story text is the real pack text (emoji dropped). Meanings: the segment text is what Ling SPEAKS; the card shows the source zh from the episode. Examples are the real pack examples. The 'hook' segment is a single-line scene_contrast (empty setup, payoff "IT'S 2 A.M."); the promise and the push-ups stay in the story. Its payoff (the whole hook text) is revealed on "It's".

segments.text: I promised my roommate I would sleep before midnight, and I said it in deadly earnest.
When the alarm sounded, they began searching in deadly earnest.
It is now 2 a.m., and I am doing push-ups in the dorm hallway.
Whether late-night training helps is debatable.
The accuracy of these figures is debatable.
It is frivolous: I wanted to see if the vending machine would still sell me a protein bar.
He made a frivolous comment during the serious meeting.
